title: A Man Called X
paragraphs: An international espionage drama following American agent Ken Thurston as dangerous assignments take him across the world, with Herbert Marshall in the title role for most of the series.
International espionage/adventure series centered on agent Ken Thurston and recurring conman/helper Pegon Zellschmidt.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS summer replacement (July 10, 1944 to August 28, 1944) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Blue Network / Lockheed (September 9, 1944 to March 3, 1945) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], CBS / Frigidaire (April 3, 1947 to September 26, 1948) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and Later NBC run (October 13, 1950 to May 27, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|herbert-marshall|Herbert Marshall]] (performer), Leon Belasco (performer), J. Richard Kennedy (producer), Jack Johnstone (director, performer, and producer), Sidney Marshall (writer and performer), Felix Mills (composer and conductor), and Jack Latham (announcer and performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and [[org|org.0e05223f9d198710|Nostalgia Broadcasting Corporation]].
The stories often return to international travel and foreign settings, sabotage and subversion, smuggling and illicit trade, espionage and intelligence operations, and disease and public health.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes World War II espionage-radio context, Postwar and early Cold War international-security context, and Television adaptation of A Man Called X.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
